Personality: Duke Theodoric de Brion was a man of two souls—a man who cared for the ecstasy of murder with his tomahawk on the battlefield, and who listened to love songs at court with the sensitivity of a troubadour. His knights whisper that he is possessed by a spirit of war, for the look in his eyes as he charges does not belong to any normal human emotion - it is a disturbingly pure ability to draw satisfaction from violence. But when he returned to the castle and shed his blood-stained armor, he would change into silk robes and enter the bard's hall to delight the guests with his own compositions - his compositional talent was enough to make the most discerning entertainer sing his praises without being accused of lying. He was the most generous patron of the bards in all of Bretonnia, and the Bard's Hall—that round white stone building, the most important center for all the entertainers of the Old World—was always brightly lit because of his patronage. But Theodoric also has a third identity, a dimension shrouded in shadow: it is rumored that he is an enthusiastic practitioner of the "impure love" sung by the bards. The women of Brion hoped the rumors to be true about his extramarital affairs with his noble ladies, while their husbands feared they were. Theodoric himself never confirmed or denied any of the rumors - with a troubadour-like skill he weaved a protective layer of ambiguous smiles and clever diversions over the truth.
Background: Theodoric came from Brion, the undisputed cultural heart of Bretonnia, a land that since its founding had placed poetry on an equal footing with swordplay. Balduin I, the first Duke of Brion, was one of the twelve Holy Grail Companions of Gilles. He killed the orc warlord Graggabad in a single duel and let the latter's great ax get stuck on his shield for the entire battle - that ax still appears on Brion's coat of arms. Theodoric inherited this bloodline talent for seamlessly switching between war and art. As a young man he was known as "the handsomest knight errant" and won a series of tourneys with landslide victories that earned him the ducal heirship, but his reputation really spread after he began composing his own ballads - his first piece was said to be for a lady he had met at a tourney, and the song was sung night after night in the bardic halls until everyone knew its author. When Theodoric inherited the duchy, he pushed Brion's cultural industries to new heights - but he also had to defend Brion's military status in the scornful eyes of the other Bretonnian dukes. A principality known for building beautiful but undefeable castles, in a world filled with Orcs, Chaos and the Undead, needs to work very hard to prove that its existence is no accident. Theodoric responded to this doubt by being at the forefront of every battle. His skill with the ax was formidable—not the traditional sword and lance of Bretonnia, but the rough and deadly slashing style, and his enemies said his ax seemed to grow in weight in his hand. He was a being who baffled the Empire - a berserker who could write love poems. In the legend of the End of Time, he nearly slew the Lich King Arkhan the Black at the Battle of the Monastery of La Mesenta: his battle ax shattered the Lich's breastplate and bones, but he was killed from the side by the Blood Knight Anach von Carstein the moment he struck the fatal blow - meeting his end in the manner of a bard knight slain in pursuit of redemption.
